title: Clean Economic Convergence: A Global Development Framework
subtitle: Integrating Economic Catch-Up, Clean Technology Diffusion, and Sustainable Structural Transformation
dek: Formalizes Clean Economic Convergence as an integrated global development framework showing how declining clean-technology costs, modern green industrial policy, and WACC compression accelerate catch-up growth and sustainable structural transformation across emerging economies through 2050.
abstract: For over half a century, development economics operated under an assumed structural trade-off: rapid income convergence required carbon-intensive heavy industrialization, while environmental stewardship constrained developing-country growth. The dramatic, empirically grounded cost collapse of modular clean technologies—solar photovoltaics, lithium-ion storage, electric mobility, precision agritech, and digital public rails—has fundamentally inverted that trade-off. Anchored to 9 live World Bank World Development Indicators spanning 2000–2025 across 24 economies and regional aggregates and 24 peer-reviewed studies in growth theory, structural transformation, directed technical change, and green industrial policy, this monograph formalizes Clean Economic Convergence as an actionable global development framework.

Live 25-year WDI baselines expose a stark divergence between high-investment industrial convergers (China 7.55%/yr, Vietnam 5.20%/yr, India 4.94%/yr, Bangladesh 4.76%/yr) and capital-constrained, prematurely deindustrializing regions (Latin America 1.31%/yr, Sub-Saharan Africa 1.36%/yr, Low-Income economies 1.19%/yr at 48.8% electricity access and 7.14 MJ/USD energy intensity). Integrating clean-technology diffusion, agricultural productivity release, green-complexity industrial policy, and multilateral WACC compression into a 2026–2050 macroeconomic simulation, this study projects a cumulative Clean Economic Convergence Dividend of USD 45 trillion to USD 78 trillion (central: USD 61.5 trillion, constant 2025 USD; 3% NPV: USD 36.4 trillion)—lifting EMDE per-capita growth by +1.4 to +2.2 percentage points annually while cutting the carbon intensity of catch-up by 55%–68%.
findings: Documents 25-year live WDI convergence baselines (2000–2025), exposing the split between high-investment Asian convergers and stalled, energy-scarce regions.
Formalizes Clean Economic Convergence by uniting directed technical change, Wright's Law clean-tech learning curves, green economic complexity, and blended-finance WACC compression.
Projects a cumulative 2026–2050 EMDE Clean Economic Convergence Dividend of USD 45T–78T (central: USD 61.5T; 3% NPV: USD 36.4T) across five sectoral channels.
keywords: clean technology diffusion and Wrights law
emerging economy cost of capital WACC
method: Empirical synthesis using verified World Bank WDI and international datasets, peer-reviewed literature, H Heuristics Cross-System Spillover (2nd–4th order) mapping, maladaptation guardrails, and quantitative 2050 polycrisis scenarios.
